powergrid.ponder.basin_heater.text_1: Kärlvärmaren kan driva ett kärl som behöver värme
powergrid.ponder.basin_heater.text_2: När den har tillräkligt med kraft kan den driva den högsta nivån av värme
powergrid.ponder.battery.text_1: Låter dig spara el för senare användning
powergrid.ponder.battery.text_2: När batteriet laddas ur, börjar dess spänning och resistans att förändras
powergrid.ponder.bell.text_1: Ringklockan är en elektrisk enhet som gör ljud när du driver den.
powergrid.ponder.carbon_pile.text_1: För att monetera en Kolstapel måste du placera kol block ovanför Kolstapel Spolen
powergrid.ponder.carbon_pile.text_2: Resistansen av Kolstapeln förändras baserat på hur mycket ström som flödar i spolen
powergrid.ponder.carbon_pile.text_3: Resistans värdena av kolstapeln stiger med höjden på strukturen
powergrid.ponder.carbon_pile.text_4: Resistansen kan också förändras med värdespanelen på toppen av kolstapeln
powergrid.ponder.ceiling_tile.text_3: Takpanelen stödjer en mängd av olika tillbehör
powergrid.ponder.circuit_capacitor.text_: Kondensatorn är en komponent som kan spara en liten mångd av elektrisitet
powergrid.ponder.circuit_cgauge.text_1: Strömmätaren kan placeras på ett kretskort.
powergrid.ponder.circuit_cgauge.text_2: När den är placerad vid en kant, kommer den att utlösa en redstone signal proportionellt till sitt mätna värde
När driven med kraft, modulen roterar ett halft nummer
När den inte längre får kraft, kommer den att rotera till nästa nummer
När modulen når slutet av sina nummer/tecken
Kommer den att stanna på en "Blank sida" och kommer inte att gå förbi det
För att återställa modulen kopplar du reset linjen till jord, och sedan ger du den pulser igen
Du kan byta de i en Krets Arbetsbänk
Du kan också byta färgen av modulen i en Krets Arbetsbänk
powergrid.ponder.circuit_electron_tube.t: Ett Elektron rör är en ikke-lineär komponent som kan förstärka signaler
För att få det att fungera, måste du först driva dess värme element
Den kommer sedan att leda ström från anoden till katoden. Denna strömmen kan be kontrollerad med Grid piggen
En negativ spänning kan tillämpas på grid piggen. En liten förändring där kan resultera i stora förändringar i anod strömmen
powergrid.ponder.circuit_label.text_1: Etiketter kan placeras på kretskort för att medge information
powergrid.ponder.circuit_label.text_2: De kommer i olika storlek och deras text och färg kan ändras
powergrid.ponder.circuit_neon.text_1: Neon Röret är en simpel enhet som lyser när du tillämpar ström till den
powergrid.ponder.circuit_neon.text_2: Den behöver en ström begränsande resistor för att inte förstöras direkt efter att den har lyst upp
powergrid.ponder.circuit_potentiometer.t: Potentiometern är en mindre version av en Rheostat
Dess resistans kan förändras genom att interagera med den
Redstone reläet kan användas för att bryta ström med en redstone signal
Den måste placeras med pilen riktad mot en kant
Regulator Röret är en enhet med ett speciellt syfte, under korrekta omständigheter kan den en medge väldigt stabil spännings referens
powergrid.ponder.circuit_relay.text_1: En Relä är en mindre version av en Kontaktor
powergrid.ponder.circuit_relay.text_2: När du ger den dess konfigurerad spänning kommer den att byta till den normalt öppna terminalen
powergrid.ponder.circuit_resistor.text_1: Resistorer är en av de mest simpla elektriska komponenter, de begränsar strömmen såm flödar genom dem.
powergrid.ponder.circuit_resistor.text_2: Du kan beräka den strömmen med hjälp av U = I * R ekvationen, där I är strömmen, U är spänning och R är resistans
powergrid.ponder.circuit_vgauge.text_1: Spänningsmätaren kan bli placerad på ett kretskort.
powergrid.ponder.circuit_vgauge.text_2: När den är placerad vid en kant, kommer den att utlösa en redstone signal proportionellt till sit mätna värde
powergrid.ponder.circuit_via.text_1: Kopparklimpar kan användas som vior på ett kretskort
powergrid.ponder.circuit_via.text_2: De är 1x1 och kan användas för att flytta spår mellan lager
powergrid.ponder.circuit_via.text_3: Vias can also be used to interconnect multiple circuit boards
powergrid.ponder.constant_speed_motor.te: A Constant Speed Motor combines the functionality of an Electric Motor and a Speed Controller
Its speed is constant while the provided voltage determines the stress capacity and rotation direction
powergrid.ponder.contactor.text_1: A Contactor lets you switch high currents with a lower voltage input.
powergrid.ponder.contactor_stack.text_2: And only one needs to be powered
powergrid.ponder.cord.text_1: Cords are 2 strand wires which can make connecting things easier
powergrid.ponder.cord.text_2: Cords can be attached to pairs of regular terminals at their ends
powergrid.ponder.cord.text_3: As well as most of consumer devices
powergrid.ponder.cord_junction.text_1: Cord junctions allow you to extend and split cords easily
powergrid.ponder.cord_socket.text_1: Cord sockets allow you to combine simple wires into cords with style
powergrid.ponder.crt.text_1: The Cathode Ray Tube is a complex device that needs a bit of setup to work
powergrid.ponder.crt.text_2: First, you need to provide 12 volts between the Heater and Cathode pins
powergrid.ponder.crt.text_3: Next, connect about 1000 volts between the Anode and Cathode
powergrid.ponder.crt.text_4: You can change the position of the dot using the deflection coils
powergrid.ponder.crt.text_5: You can apply a negative voltage to the Grid to change brightness of the trace
powergrid.ponder.current_gauge.header: Monitoring Electricity using the Current Gauge
powergrid.ponder.current_gauge.text_1: The Current Gauge displays the current flowing through it's terminals
powergrid.ponder.current_gauge.text_2: Current gauges are in series with the circuit so they can have an effect on the transferred power
powergrid.ponder.current_gauge.text_3: If you were to connect it in parallel, huge currents might flow which can potentially damage the meter or nearby equipment
powergrid.ponder.device_connector.text_1: Some devices don't directly expose their electrical terminals
powergrid.ponder.device_connector.text_2: To power them, you'll have to place a Device Connector and attach your wires to it
powergrid.ponder.device_connector.text_3: The Device Connector can also be used to power Forge Energy and Create: The Factory Must Grow devices (if installed)
powergrid.ponder.electric_fan.text_1: The Electric Fan Moves Air Using Electricity
powergrid.ponder.electric_fan.text_2: Direction and Speed Are Dependent on the Voltage Applied
powergrid.ponder.electric_fan.text_3: Fans Can Blow Air Over Hot Components to Cool Them Down
powergrid.ponder.electric_motor.text_1: The electric motor lets you convert electricity into rotation
powergrid.ponder.electric_motor.text_2: The speed of the motor depends on the voltage you provide
powergrid.ponder.electromagnet.text_1: The Electromagnet can process items provided beneath it
powergrid.ponder.electromagnet.text_2: The Input items can be dropped or placed on a Depot under the Electromagnet
powergrid.ponder.electromagnet.text_3: When items are provided on a belt...
powergrid.ponder.electromagnet.text_4: The Electromagnet will hold and process them automatically
powergrid.ponder.encased_fan.text_1: Fans Can Be Used to Cool Off Hot Components
powergrid.ponder.energy_meter.header: Monitoring Electricity usage with the Energy Meter
powergrid.ponder.energy_meter.text_1: This energy meter measures energy used over time
powergrid.ponder.energy_meter.text_2: In the GUI you can see the usage in Wh or kWh by hovering over the gauges
powergrid.ponder.energy_meter.text_3: Caution, changing out the unit of measurement does not affect the previously measured value and only affects future measurements
powergrid.ponder.energy_meter.text_4: The energy meter emits a redstone pulse through a comparator every 1 Wh or kWh depending on which mode it's set to
powergrid.ponder.energy_meter.text_5: You can also reverse the power and it will count backwards
powergrid.ponder.factory_light.text_1: Right-click to add any light bulb
powergrid.ponder.factory_light_connect.t: Factory Lights can be connected to adjacent ones like this
powergrid.ponder.factory_light_tall.head: Using the Factory Light for tall buildings
powergrid.ponder.factory_light_tall.text: A Factory light can provide a light level of 15 to the top face of a block up to 16 blocks below it
powergrid.ponder.fuse.text_1: A fuse can be used to protect your devices from too much current
powergrid.ponder.fuse.text_2: It will burn if the current exceeds the set value
powergrid.ponder.generator_1.text_1: A Generator consists of two main parts
powergrid.ponder.generator_1.text_2: The Stator, built out of Coils strung on Shafts (and optionally Housings)
powergrid.ponder.generator_1.text_3: This part generates a magnetic field, through a process called Excitation
powergrid.ponder.generator_1.text_4: As well as the Armature, built out of Rotors, a Commutator, and a Clutch
powergrid.ponder.generator_1.text_5: This is where electricity is generated. In typical setups, electrical load should be connected to the commutator.
powergrid.ponder.generator_1.text_6: To start generating electricity you must provide an Excitation Current to the Stator, through a Device Connector
powergrid.ponder.generator_1.text_7: Now lets crank up the voltage!
powergrid.ponder.generator_2.text_1: At this point you might have thought of a small problem.
powergrid.ponder.generator_2.text_10: 2.Resistance - The 'excitation loop resistance' must be low enough to allow for the field to build up, but not too low as to not overpower the coils.
powergrid.ponder.generator_2.text_11: 3.Rotation speed - The generator must spin fast enough to generate enough of the initial starting current and build up the field.
powergrid.ponder.generator_2.text_2: How do you provide excitation current if you have no other power source?
powergrid.ponder.generator_2.text_3: This is where the concept of Self-Excitation comes into play.
powergrid.ponder.generator_2.text_4: The stator coils posses a small residual magnetic field which can be used to start a feedback reaction.
powergrid.ponder.generator_2.text_5: To have better control of the output voltage, we'll use a Rheostat.
powergrid.ponder.generator_2.text_8: A self-excited generator is sensitive to a couple of factors.
powergrid.ponder.generator_2.text_9: 1.Rotation direction - The generator will only work when spinning one way, stator wiring must be flipped for it to work the other way.
powergrid.ponder.generator_3.text_1: Generator voltage will drop when a load is connected
powergrid.ponder.generator_3.text_2: This effect can be reduced by utilizing the Carbon Pile Regulator
powergrid.ponder.generator_3.text_3: Without any extra connections, the carbon pile is just a simple resistor.
powergrid.ponder.generator_clutch.text_1: The Generator Clutch is the base of all generator assemblies
powergrid.ponder.generator_clutch.text_2: It provides a weak coupling between your kinetic network and the generator shaft
powergrid.ponder.generator_clutch.text_3: You can use a redstone signal to change the coupling strength
powergrid.ponder.generator_housing.text_: The generator housing can be used to connect windings around a rotor
This allows for a cleaner generator setup with less wires connected around rotors
powergrid.ponder.generator_rotor.text_1: Rotors are the most basic part of a generator assembly, they generate electricity when spinning in a magnetic field.
powergrid.ponder.generator_rotor.text_2: You can extend the rotor assembly by placing more rotor blocks
powergrid.ponder.generator_winding.text_: Right-Clicking two shafts with a coil item will create a winding
powergrid.ponder.grounding.text_1: The grounding rod provides a 0V ground reference to your grid
powergrid.ponder.grounding.text_2: You can use it to transfer power but you must be careful...
powergrid.ponder.grounding.text_3: High potential and bad ground conditions will cause the ground to become electrified and cause damage to nearby entities.
powergrid.ponder.growth_lamp.text_1: The growth lamp is a special type of light bulb which accelerates crop growth in a certain area when powered on
powergrid.ponder.heating_coil_basic.head: Warming up the atmosphere
powergrid.ponder.heating_coil_basic.text: The heating coil can be used to heat up the passing Air Flow if enough power is applied to it
By applying a bigger voltage the Air Flow can be used for bulk blasting
powergrid.ponder.heating_coil_speed.head: Electrified bulk processing
powergrid.ponder.heating_coil_speed.text: The heating coil allows for faster bulk processing
powergrid.ponder.hv_breaker.text_1: HV Breaker can be used to safely switch a high power load
powergrid.ponder.hv_breaker.text_2: To close it, you must first wind it up
powergrid.ponder.hv_breaker.text_3: Its state can then be toggled with a redstone pulse
powergrid.ponder.hv_breaker.text_4: The breaker can be opened without having to wind it up again
powergrid.ponder.hv_switch.text_1: The High Voltage Switch allows you to toggle electricity using a kinetic input
powergrid.ponder.improved_grounding.head: Better ground reference
powergrid.ponder.improved_grounding.text: Regular blocks are not that conductive and will cause your grounding rod to have a high impedance
You can improve the ground conditions by adding conductive blocks close to the grounding rod
powergrid.ponder.insulated_wire.text_1: Insulated wires can be colored by right clicking them with a dye or by holding a dye in your offhand while placing them.
powergrid.ponder.light.header: Lighting up the world with electricity
powergrid.ponder.light.text_1: When light bulbs are inserted into fixtures and powered on they turn electricity into light
powergrid.ponder.light.text_2: If the voltage is not high enough, the light bulb will be dimmer
powergrid.ponder.light.text_3: You can change the color of the light bulb by right-clicking it with a dye
powergrid.ponder.lightning_attractor.tex: You can build a lightning attractor using lightning rods and wool placed on a Mechanical Bearing
When you spin it fast enough during a thunderstorm it will make lightning strikes more frequent
powergrid.ponder.modular_display.text_1: You can place modules in by clicking a display module on a empty slot
powergrid.ponder.modular_display.text_2: You can remove them by shift clicking
powergrid.ponder.modular_display.text_3: There is a case ground in the center and a positive and reset pin for every slot
powergrid.ponder.modular_display.text_4: See display module ponder for instructions on how to use the modules
powergrid.ponder.modular_display.text_5: You can click and hold on a slot that has a module to change what the module displays
powergrid.ponder.modular_display.text_6: You can dye modules by clicking the slot with dye
powergrid.ponder.parallel_generator_wind: Windings placed next to each other will connect in series
This allows for a cleaner generator setup with less wires connected around rotors
powergrid.ponder.plotter.text_1: The Plotter is a simple electromechanical device that measures voltage over time
powergrid.ponder.plotter.text_2: The graph color can be changed by right clicking the plotter with a dye
powergrid.ponder.power_gauge.header: Monitoring Electricity using the Power Gauge
powergrid.ponder.power_gauge.text_1: The Power Gauge can be used to measure power going into a section of the electrical network
powergrid.ponder.power_resistor.text_1: The Power Resistor is a simple device which lets you limit the current flow in a circuit.
powergrid.ponder.power_resistor.text_2: You can change the resistance by clicking on its top
powergrid.ponder.power_resistor.text_3: The current flow is equal to the voltage across the resistor divided by its resistance (I = V / R)
powergrid.ponder.punch_card_reader.text_: The Punch Card Reader is a device that can be used to playback a sequence of signals.
It will connect the common terminal to an output pin when a hole is read from the card.
To work, the device needs a kinetic input. Rotation speed controls the read speed.
Punch Cards can be inserted manually or automatically.
powergrid.ponder.redstone_converter.head: Reading redstone
powergrid.ponder.redstone_converter.text: The Redstone Converter is a device that converts redstone signals into resistance changes
Its internal structure resembles that of a potentiometer
Resistance between non-inverting and tap pads will go down with the applied signal...
...while resistance between inverting and tap pads will go up
When attached to a block it'll act similar to a Redstone Comparator
For some blocks, the Redstone Converter can provide more precision than a Redstone Comparator
powergrid.ponder.rheostat.text_1: A rheostat can be used to vary electrical resistance using a kinetic input
powergrid.ponder.servo.text_1: A Servo can be used to precisely control mechanical movements using an electric signal
powergrid.ponder.servo.text_2: The control pin accepts a voltage between -5 and 5 volts, which maps to -360 and 360 degrees of rotation
powergrid.ponder.shared.gauge_customize: You can change how the measured value is displayed by right-clicking the gauge with a name tag
powergrid.ponder.shared.gauge_goggles: When wearing Engineers' Goggles, the player can get more detailed information from the Gauge
powergrid.ponder.shared.gauge_range: You can change the gauge's range by clicking on top of it
powergrid.ponder.solar_panel_bearing.tex: The Solar Panel Bearing attaches to Solar Panels placed in front of it.
For example this contraption has 6 Solar Panels attached it would give you 4 options (1x6, 2x3, 3x2, 6x1).
The first number shows how many strings you have in parallel, and the second number is how many Solar Panels you have in a string.
In simplified terms the further the slider is to the left you get more voltage and less current and further to the right is more current less voltage.
The max amount of panels in a string is 25, if your Solar Panel amount isn't divisible by 1-9 with a quotient of less than 26 it will not assemble.
The fix is to add or remove Solar Panels.
By clicking you can assemble the contraption.
You do not need to glue Solar Panels together as long as they are touching.
If you do not connect the Solar Panels directly to the face then you need to glue every block that isn't a Solar Panel and glue at least one Solar Panel.
Gluing like this will only turn the center.
Gluing like this will rotate the center and the Solar Panels.
When assembled the output of all connected Solar Panels is combined on the terminals on the bearing.
On the side of the block you can change how the power from the Solar Panels is output.
The output is in (Strings in parallel * Panels in String).
The Solar Panel needs to point at the sun to make power.
Biome placement matters, the hotter the Solar Panel gets the less efficient it is.
Placing the Solar Panel in the desert will get you noticeably less overall power than...
Placing one in a plains biome.
Solar panels placed next to each other can connect to form a multiblock.
Next scene will show you how to start making power with Solar Panels.
The closer to directly pointing at the sun you get, the more power the panel will make.
For pointing with more accuracy you can use the Solar Panel Bearing refer to that ponder for more information.
The Solar Panel needs direct sunlight.
If there are any obstacles in the way it will make substantially less power.
There are some blocks that let light through like glass, water, leaves and a few other blocks.
powergrid.ponder.solar_panel_power_creat: A Solar Panels output is based on an IV curve, Google "Solar Panel IV curve" for an image of a general IV curve.
There are a few terms you need to know.
Voc is the max voltage of the Solar Panel with no load on it.
Isc is the short current of the Solar Panel aka the current you would get placing a wire between the positive and negative.
Vmp and Imp are the points along the IV curve where the Solar Panel makes the most power, these points shift around depending on the environmental conditions of the Solar Panel.
A simple way to use a Solar Panel is by impedance matching it to your load.
For example if a Solar Panels Vmp is 21.2V and Imp is 7.8A, Ohm's law dictates that the optimal load resistance would be 2.71 Ohms.
The further you get from that resistance the less overall power the panel will make.
powergrid.ponder.string_lights.text_1: The String Light Cord is a decorative wire that will light up when powered
powergrid.ponder.string_lights.text_2: Its pattern can be changed by combining it with any amount of dyes in the crafting table.
powergrid.ponder.switch_lv_button.text_1: Switches and buttons allow you to manually toggle electricity
powergrid.ponder.switch_lv_switch.text_1: Switches and buttons allow you to manually toggle electricity
powergrid.ponder.switch_mv_switch.text_1: Switches and buttons allow you to manually toggle electricity
powergrid.ponder.tag.ceiling_tile_attach: Blocks which can be placed on the ceiling tile
Components which can be placed on a circuit
powergrid.ponder.tag.electric_devices.de: Components which use electricity to do something
powergrid.ponder.tag.electric_relays.des: Components which help guide electricity in the right direction
Components which can be used to build a generator
powergrid.ponder.thunder_magnet.text_1: When lightning strikes near an iron ingot it has a chance to magnetize it
powergrid.ponder.transformer_nether.head: Interdimensional transformers
powergrid.ponder.transformer_nether.text: Assembling a transformer next to a nether portal...
...will create a linked transformer on the other end.
powergrid.ponder.transformer_sizes.text_: Transformers come in different sizes, each of them offering different power capabilities and winding capacities
powergrid.ponder.transformer_winding.tex: To wind a transformer, first select the starting terminal for your winding
Next, click on the transformer body and pick the number of turn you want to add
Lastly, select the end terminal for your winding
Your transformer will now transform voltage with the ratio you wound
powergrid.ponder.variac.text_1: A variac can be used to variably transform voltages using a kinetic input
powergrid.ponder.voltage_gauge.header: Monitoring Electricity using the Voltage Gauge
powergrid.ponder.voltage_gauge.text_1: The Voltage Gauge displays the voltage potential between it's terminals
powergrid.ponder.voltage_gauge.text_2: It connects in parallel to your circuit
powergrid.ponder.voltage_gauge.text_3: If you were to connect it in series, virtually no current would be able to flow
powergrid.ponder.wire_connector.text_1: Wire connectors can be used as attachment points for wires
powergrid.ponder.wire_connector.text_2: They serve no purpose other than routing wires
powergrid.ponder.wire_loop.text_1: Current will not flow unless the circuit forms a complete loop
powergrid.ponder.wire_simple.text_1: Wires are used to transfer electricity between terminals of electric devices
powergrid.ponder.wire_voltage_drop.text_: Every wire has a resistance, the longer the wire, the more resistance it has
This causes a voltage drop to occur when current is flowing
Lost power is turned into heat
If too much power is drawn, the wires can overheat and break
